emergencyNumber: 995 (ambulance/fire), 999 (police — only for life-threatening emergencies; use 1800-255-0000 for non-emergency police)
healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private universal healthcare. Residents have Medisave (medical savings account) and optional insurance (MediShield). Tourists pay full costs out-of-pocket or via travel insurance. Singapore has excellent public and private hospitals.
qualityNotes: Singapore has one of the best healthcare systems in the world. Both public and private hospitals are excellent with internationally trained doctors and universally English-speaking staff. Singapore is a major medical tourism hub. Healthcare is expensive — among the highest in Asia — but quality is exceptional.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 10am-10pm daily. Guardian, Watsons, and Unity (government-run) pharmacy chains are widely available. Some 24-hour pharmacies exist. Hospital pharmacies are also available for specific needs.
pharmacyTips: Many common OTC medications are available. Singapore has strict pharmaceutical regulations — some medications available OTC elsewhere require prescriptions here. Generic medications are available. Hospital pharmacies serve specific patient needs. Chemist shops are easy to find in malls.
prescriptionRules: Singapore has strict prescription requirements. Medications prescribed by foreign doctors are NOT automatically accepted — a Singapore doctor may need to re-prescribe. Controlled substances require Singaporean authorization. Some common medications (like certain antihistamines) are available OTC.

restrictedMeds.name: Diazepam (Valium) and benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Requires Singaporean prescription or authorization from the Health Sciences Authority (HSA). Bring your foreign prescription and doctor's letter. Singapore customs is very strict about controlled substances.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Small quantities for personal use may be allowed with documentation, but a Singaporean prescription is safer.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires prescription or HSA authorization. Singapore takes a zero-tolerance approach to drug trafficking.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Requires Singaporean prescription or special authorization from HSA. Contact the Singaporean embassy before traveling with ADHD medications. Penalties for unauthorized possession are severe.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in Singapore — severe penalties including death for trafficking. There are no exceptions. Do not bring any cannabis products, including CBD.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For any potentially controlled medications, carry the original prescription and HSA authorization if required. Declare all medications at customs.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not required but strongly recommended. Singapore is extremely expensive for healthcare.
travelInsurance.tips: Singapore is one of the world's most expensive cities for healthcare. A hospital stay can cost 500-2,000+ SGD per day. A specialist consultation costs 100-250 SGD. Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is strongly recommended — serious emergencies may require evacuation to another country.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers from most countries. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Singapore is dengue-endemic — take mosquito precautions (use repellent, wear long sleeves at dusk).

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Singapore. Tap water is treated and meets WHO standards. Bottled water is also widely available.
foodSafetyTips: Singapore has excellent food safety standards. Hawker centers (outdoor food courts) are held to strict hygiene standards — the government regularly inspects them. Singapore's hawker food is generally very safe. Water and ice in drinks are safe at licensed establishments.
medicalTourismNote: Singapore is Asia's premier medical tourism destination — known for cardiac surgery, cancer treatment, organ transplants, and complex procedures. Quality rivals the best in the world. Costs are high by regional standards but competitive with Western countries for complex procedures.
metaDescription: Health & medication guide for Singapore. Emergency numbers (995/999), pharmacy tips, restricted medications (strict drug laws), travel insurance, water safety, and vaccination recommendations.

hospitals.name: Singapore General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Singapore's flagship hospital. Largest acute care hospital.

hospitals.name: Mount Elizabeth Hospital
hospitals.notes: Premier private hospital on Orchard Road. International patient center.

hospitals.name: Raffles Hospital
hospitals.notes: Private hospital with 24-hour emergency and traveler's clinic.

hospitals.name: Gleneagles Hospital
hospitals.notes: Part of Parkway Health. International patient services.

dentalCare.availability: World-class dental care available. Singapore is known for exceptional medical and dental quality.
dentalCare.costRange: SGD $50-150 for consultation; SGD $100-400 for fillings; SGD $150-500 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Singapore dental care is expensive but among the best in Asia. Many clinics offer same-day appointments. Q&M Dental is the largest chain.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: National Dental Centre Singapore handles complex dental emergencies. Hospital emergency departments at SGH and NUH also provide dental emergency care.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Widely available. English is an official language. Many international therapists and counselors practice in Singapore.
mentalHealth.notes: Singapore has good mental health services. IMH (Institute of Mental Health) is the main public facility. Private therapists charge SGD $150-300 per session.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Singapore is one of the most accessible cities in Asia. Strict building codes ensure wheelchair access in modern buildings. Excellent accessible public transport.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: All hospitals are fully wheelchair accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: MRT (subway) is fully accessible with elevators and platform screen doors. All public buses are wheelchair accessible. Accessible taxis available through booking.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Gardens by the Bay, Sentosa, and most attractions are wheelchair accessible. Hawker centres may have limited space. SG Enable provides accessibility resources.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates. Voluntary use in healthcare settings.
covidStatus.testing: ART tests at pharmacies (SGD $5-10). PCR at clinics (SGD $60-120).
covidStatus.notes: Singapore removed all COVID restrictions. Dengue is a more significant ongoing health concern.

insuranceClaimProcess: Singapore hospitals are efficient with insurance documentation. Most private hospitals offer direct billing with international insurers. Keep all receipts and Medisave/insurance claim forms. Hospitals provide English documentation as standard.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private or international facilities. Public-system rates can be much lower (or free for residents). Actual costs vary by city, facility, and exchange rate.

medicalEvacuation.primaryDestination: Singapore is itself the regional medical hub
medicalEvacuation.note: Local hospitals handle the vast majority of cases — air evacuation is rarely needed for tourists. If a condition exceeds local capacity: Singapore is the leading medical hub for Southeast and South Asia. Mount Elizabeth, Raffles, and Gleneagles handle the most complex cases in the region.
